mission_3.prediction:
Repulsion only (open map): with influence distance fixed at 1.0 m, I raised repulsion strength from 0.7 (social_1) to 1.3. Both previews stayed "succeeded". The path near the person at (0, -1.7) bent a little farther away and got slightly longer (about 13.6 m to 13.7 m, baseline 13.5 m). The change is small because the bottom wall limits how far the route can move, so the closest pass stays at about 0.75 m body clearance.

Influence distance only (open map): keeping repulsion at 1.3, I raised influence distance from 1.0 m to 1.5 m (social_2). The status stayed "succeeded" and the detour became clearly wider: the path starts bending earlier and is about 14.6 m long, with more of the route near x = 0 kept around 0.8 to 0.9 m from the person instead of 0.75 to 0.8 m.

The same change on the constrained map: social_1 (0.7, 1.0 m) succeeded, but social_2 (1.3, 1.5 m) showed "oscillation". The dashed line stops partway because, in the narrow passage, the wall avoidance and the larger repulsion keep cancelling the attraction to the next waypoint, so the robot kept oscillating instead of moving forward.

I also tried repulsion 2.0 with influence 1.5 m on the open map, and it oscillated there too. So larger repulsion or influence moves the route farther from the person only until there is no room left, then the field gets stuck.
mission_3.comparison:
A*: social_2 (repulsion 1.3, influence 1.5 m) had the largest minimum_person_clearance_m, 0.84 m, with 0.0 s of personal_space_s. Its baseline had 0.76 m and 0.0 s. social_2 did not cost time or distance: 46.5 s and 13.1 m vs 46.7 s and 13.2 m for baseline, even though the refined plan was about 1 m longer (14.6 m vs 13.5 m), because the controller cuts the smoothed corners. Surprisingly, social_1 was worse than baseline: 0.71 m clearance and 1.8 s inside the 0.75 m threshold at up to 0.30 m/s. Its weak repulsion only shifted the path slightly, and the executed route (an AMCL estimate, not ground truth) passed a little closer than planned.

RRT: the baseline had the largest clearance, 1.73 m, with 0.0 s personal_space_s. social_1 (1.71 m) and social_2 (1.73 m) are within a few centimetres of it, which is localization noise. The planned lengths were identical (12.47 m) because RRT's random route already passed more than 1.5 m from the person, outside both influence distances, so the field had nothing to repel. Times were 44.4 s baseline, 43.4 s social_1 and 44.0 s social_2, with distances all about 11.5 to 11.6 m, so there was no real time or distance cost either way.
mission_3.recommendation:
I would keep A* with social_2 (repulsion 1.3, influence 1.5 m) for this scenario. It succeeded with a minimum person clearance of 0.84 m and 0.0 s inside the 0.75 m personal-space threshold, taking 46.5 s and 13.1 m. The A* baseline succeeded in a similar 46.7 s and 13.2 m but passed closer (0.76 m), only just outside the threshold, and the weaker social_1 setting actually entered personal space for 1.8 s (0.71 m). So social_2 gave the most space for no measurable time or distance cost, and A* is deterministic, so the planned route is repeatable. RRT kept even more space (1.73 m), but only because its random route happened to take a different corridor. A different seed could pass much closer, and the field had no effect on it.

The person here never moves, so the field is computed once on a fixed position. A walking person can step into the refined route after it is planned, and the robot would need to replan or slow down and wait, which this fixed-path experiment does not test. The trials also do not measure how comfortable a real person feels, whether they would prefer the robot to pass in front of or behind them, or how they react to its speed.
